reason: The capillary sleeves show an empty inner face suited to the endothelial lining, making this a clear first vessel component.

effect: The arterial wall and lining formed branching arterial vessels; the capillary bed still needs a return route.

reason: The pocket-shaped valve folds belong inside the vein.
expectation: The veins should gain valves that help prevent backward flow.

effect: The veins now have valves, and the picture shows how muscle compression helps return blood toward the heart.
reaction: The forward and backward arrows make the valves’ role clear.
reason: Arteries deliver blood to capillary beds, so connecting those is the next part of the route.
expectation: The arterial vessels should connect to the capillary network.

effect: The arteries now lead through arterioles into the capillary network; the venous return remains to be connected.
reaction: The parallel branches make the broad tissue coverage clear.
reason: The venous return should complete the route from the capillary bed back toward the heart.
expectation: The capillaries should connect to veins, completing the tissue vessel route.

effect: The capillaries now connect to veins, completing the systemic vessel route and the chapter goal.
reaction: The completed route is satisfying, though the final picture description is brief.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding venous valves was most worthwhile: the planned muscle-compression and flow arrows connect their structure to returning blood toward the heart.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the lined veins was fairly predictable and its picture description added little beyond the visible wall and lining.

surprise.text: The valve result made the role of contracting limb muscle in venous return explicit, rather than showing valves alone.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the vessel components and final connections followed the stated goal. The term pericytes appeared in the capillary-sleeve description without explaining their role.

continue.text: I would continue to see how this vessel network connects to the heart and tissue exchange; the assembly made the route clear, although some steps were predictable.
